items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to design synthetic TnpB gene-editing enzymes (SynTnpBs) that outperform their natural counterparts, reaching up to 46-50% editing efficiency in human cells versus 28% for the original. Published in Science, the work shows generative models can invent new gene-editing tools with properties evolution never produced, expanding the CRISPR toolbox.

A University of Manchester team developed a physics-informed machine-learning method that hunts for two-dimensional 'flat-band' quantum materials, screening over 10,000 candidates with 98.2% accuracy. The approach replaces slow density-functional-theory calculations, dramatically speeding the search for exotic quantum materials.

A look inside David Baker's Institute for Protein Design, where a 100+ researcher lab and its open 'communal brain' of deep-learning tools (RFdiffusion and successors) now design proteins from scratch with atomic precision. The piece maps how AI-driven protein design is reshaping how biotech invents antibodies, enzymes and medicines.

An open AI competition to predict drug metabolism (whether compounds activate the PXR receptor that clears roughly half of all marketed drugs) ended in a 28-way statistical tie, with startup Inductive Bio narrowly on top. The result suggests data quality, not raw model size, drives performance in AI-for-drug-discovery, reshaping how the field benchmarks its models.

Tel Aviv University researchers built GOFLOW, an AI system that reconstructs fine-scale ocean surface currents from satellite thermal imagery, revealing small-scale dynamics that standard models miss. Better maps of these currents sharpen climate, weather and ocean-atmosphere gas-exchange predictions.
